title: Paridyum test evidence envelope, version 1
description: One test job's report. STD-0014 is the standard; this is its machine contract. A test run produces JUnit, which describes which assertions ran and is anonymous about everything else — repository, commit, tier, which declared test type it implements, and whether a person or a workflow produced it. This envelope carries those, and wraps the JUnit rather than replacing it. Nothing here parses test names or messages: those are prose, and branching on them is ANTI-0008.

schema.description: A consumer that does not recognise the major version REFUSES the envelope rather than reading the fields it happens to recognise.

commit.description: Full SHA. Not abbreviated: an abbreviation is ambiguous across a ledger meant to outlive the run.

ref.description: Full ref. refs/pull/N/merge and refs/heads/main say different things about what was tested and must stay distinguishable.

tier.description: STD-0008's tiers, spelled as test-registry.yaml spells them.

implements.description: Declared test types this job implements. MAY be empty, and empty is a claim — this job implements no declared type — never a way to say 'unknown'. Omitting the field is invalid for that reason.

stack.description: From class-registry.yaml's stack vocabulary, plus `none` for a job that is not language-specific. `python` is declared before any Python repository exists, so the first one does not need a schema change.

provenance.description: `ci` means a workflow produced it and its run can be inspected. `local` means one person's machine. A local envelope may never satisfy a gate, and may never be the sole reason a required type reports as running — see STD-0014.

run.description: Required when provenance is `ci`. Identity of the workflow run, so the envelope can be traced to logs that outlive it.

url.description: A pattern, not `format: uri`. The estate's validator implements only `format: date`, so `format: uri` advertised a constraint nothing checked — found 2026-08-21 and fixed in both places.

submitted_by.description: Required when provenance is `local`. Operator identifier as registry/operators.yaml spells it. A local result with no author is an anonymous claim.

started_at.description: RFC 3339, UTC, Z. Not local time: a ledger spanning machines cannot order local timestamps.

outcome.description: `errored` is the job failing to run its tests at all, which is not the same as tests failing. Collapsing the two hides infrastructure decay.

totals.description: Counts. The four outcomes must sum to `tests`; a consumer that finds otherwise refuses the envelope rather than guessing which is wrong.

artifacts.description: Where the raw evidence went, with a digest so a later copy can be checked against what was reported. May be empty.

skipped_reason.description: Required in substance when outcome is `skipped`. Free text FOR A PERSON and never branched on. A skip with no reason is indistinguishable from a pass downstream, which is how coverage disappears quietly.
